character_sheet: A tameable baby dragon: a 5x4x10 torso with two back scales, a raked neck to a two-piece head with a jaw, two nostril nubs, three head scales and two two-piece horns, two zero-thickness 10x4 wings on root nubs, four legs of an upper, a lower and a paw, and a tail of a base, a second piece and two tip pieces with a scale (SpyroModel.java:102-285, 37 parts), drawn at x0.75. 200 HP, speed 0.3, 5 damage (EntitySpyro.java:115-120). Beef tames it one time in two (:225-241); its owner can untame it with a dead bush, put its fire out with ice, light it with flint and steel, name it, sit it with any other item, or evolve it into a Dragon with a diamond (:247-328) - one tick in 100,000 it grows up on its own (:167-187). On the ground (activity 1) it wanders, follows its owner and flees monsters (:91-100); in the air (the synched DATA_ACTIVITY at 2, :65-66, :129-136 - a 1-in-8 roll on a 1-in-100 tick, a flying owner, or an owner more than 16 blocks away, :202-205, :349-362) it flies from block target to block target near its owner (:423-473), hunts monsters within 12 blocks (:389-417, :489-507), bites within 3 blocks plus half the target's width for 5 (:405-408) and, within 8 blocks with its fire lit (DATA_SPYRO_FIRE :67-68), shoots small fireballs (:409-411, :480-487); it takes no fall damage (:210-213). It spawns in daylight above y 50 (:579-584; ModEntities.java:566-567). Read it as a dragon hatchling: a bouncy four-legged trot with the wings flapping, the legs tucked in flight, the tail held bent to one side at rest.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig (SpyroRenderer.java:23, :36; shadow 0.4875, :25) on a 64x64 sheet (SpyroModel.java:287), spyro.png (SpyroRenderer.java:19); the hitbox is 0.5 x 0.5 (ModEntities.java:566-567). The original's ModelSpyro(0.65f) argument was a wingspeed the port's model does not keep: every rhythm's frequency is multiplied by limbSwingAmount itself (SpyroModel.java:292), so the tempo rises with the walking speed. The tail's second piece is placed 3 px along the base each tick (:343-344) - key the joint, not the position.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: legs: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1, at a tempo of 2.0 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick (2.0 at full stride); every piece of a leg by the same angle about its rest, the right front and left back one way, the left front and right back the other; 0 below the threshold and in activity 3; in flight (activity 2) the front legs hold -1.0 and the back legs +1.0 plus their rests, still. Wings: pi x 0.4 = 1.257 rad (72 deg) x the speed above the same threshold, at a tempo of 2.3 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick, the right wing the negative; halved in activity 3; 0 below the threshold
groups.plain: the four legs trot in diagonal pairs, each a stiff chain, and the two wing planes flap together, all faster and wider as it walks faster; in the air the legs tuck - the front legs back, the back legs forward - and hold, while the wings still follow only the walking speed
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 2.0 * amount) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0 (activity 3: 0); activity != 2 ? (LegRightFrontTop = a - 0.087, LegRightFrontBottom = a - 0.17, RightFrontPaw = a, the left front = -a + rests, LegRightBackBottom = -a + 0.139, LegRightBackTop = -a - 0.174, RightBackPaw = -a, the left back = a + rests) : (front pieces = -1.0 + rests; back pieces = 1.0 + rests); w = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 2.3 * amount) * pi * 0.4 * amount : 0; activity == 3 ? w /= 2; WingLeft.zRot = w; WingRight.zRot = -w
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ACTIVITY int (EntitySpyro.java:65-66): 2 selects the leg tuck; 3 halves the wings and stills the legs (a value the port's entity never sets: :350-360, :393, :400 write 1 and 2); one gait group per rig is the generator's rule, so the legs and wings share this group
groups.omega_note: the frequency terms are 2.0 x limbSwingAmount for the legs and 2.3 x limbSwingAmount for the wings (SpyroModel.java:292, :295, :302): at full stride the natural periods are 3.14 and 2.73 ticks; the reference clip's fixed limbSwingAmount sets both amplitude and tempo

groups.name: tail
groups.axis: y (and the second piece's x / z position)
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) at the base and 1.6x (72 deg) at the second piece and tips, at a tempo of 1.2 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick — so at rest the cosine sits at 1 and the tail is HELD bent 45 / 72 degrees to one side, wagging only as it moves; 0 (straight) while sitting or in activity 3; the second piece is placed 3 px along the base's yaw, 0.5 to the side
groups.plain: the tail wags side to side with the walk, the tip swinging wider than the root; standing still it stays cocked to one side; sitting, it straightens
groups.math: a = (sitting || activity == 3) ? 0 : cos(t * 1.2 * amount) * pi * 0.25; TailBack.yRot = ScaleTailPiece.yRot = a; TailFront.z = TailBack.z + cos(a) * 3; TailFront.x = TailBack.x + sin(a) * 3 - 0.5; TailFront.yRot = TailPieceLarge.yRot = TailPieceSmall.yRot = a * 1.6; the tip pieces ride TailFront's position
groups.phase: isInSittingPose (the owner's sit toggle, EntitySpyro.java:325-328) and activity 3 zero it
groups.omega_note: the frequency term is 1.2 x limbSwingAmount (:292, :337): at full stride the natural period is 5.24 ticks; at rest there is no period - the tail holds cos(0) = 1

behaviour: Every rhythm's frequency is multiplied by limbSwingAmount (SpyroModel.java:292): the faster it walks, the faster it moves. Above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 the four legs trot 45 degrees x the speed in diagonal pairs (:302-319) and the two wing planes flap 72 degrees x the speed (:295-300); the tail wags 45 degrees at the base and 72 at the tip (:337-351). Standing still the legs and wings freeze and the tail is held cocked 45 degrees to one side - the cosine of zero (:337, :341).

Two state branches on the synched DATA_ACTIVITY int (EntitySpyro.java:65-66): in flight (2) the legs tuck and hold - the front pair back a radian, the back pair forward a radian (SpyroModel.java:320-335) - while the wings still beat only with the walking speed (:295); a third value (3) halves the wings, stills the legs and straightens the tail (:297, :303-304, :338-339) but the port's entity never sets it (EntitySpyro.java:350-360, :393, :400 write 1 and 2). The sitting pose straightens the tail (:338-340).

The head - both head pieces, the jaw, the nostrils, the three head scales and both horns - takes the full look yaw and pitch, the horns splayed 0.785 rad (:353-377). The torso, neck, wing root nubs and back scales are static.

The takeoff is a flag flip (EntitySpyro.java:204, :352-353, :360, :393, :400), the landing a 1-in-100 roll that mostly answers 1 (:351-353), the bite doHurtTarget within 3 blocks plus half the target's width on the flight pass (:405-408), the fireball shootFireball (:480-487) - none of them animation events.
